item.title: Fantastic Foden Fires Man City To Win Over AEK Athen
item.description: Phil Foden hit a hat-trick to underline his long-awaited return to form as Manchester City crushed AEK Athens 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday. After a significant dip over the last two seasons, Foden provided hope of a renaissance for the England playmaker with a sublime display at the Etihad Stadium. The 26-year-old, who has admitted struggling with mental health issues, hadn’t scored for 10 months prior to his goal in Saturday’s win against Ipswich. Long heralded as one of England’s brightest talents, Foden was left out of his country’s World Cup squad earlier this year in a damning sign of his fall from grace. Having ended his run without a goal in the Champions League since November 2025, Foden now has to produce nights like this on a regular basis to complete his revival. Elliot Anderson put City ahead early in the first half with his first goal for the club since his close-season move from Nottingham Forest. Foden doubled City’s lead before the break and although Stavros Pilios pulled one back for the Greek side after the interval, the Premier League leaders finished with a flourish. Rayan Cherki bagged City’s third goal in typically flamboyant fashion and Foden struck twice more to complete his treble. It was City’s second win in the league phase after beating Porto in their opening game and losing to holders Paris Saint-Germain last week. City’s future remains in limbo as they wait the result of their appeal against an independent commission’s verdict that they were guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules. item.title: PSG late show downs Barca in Champions League, Liverpool fight back
item.description: Holders Paris Saint-Germain made it three wins from three in this season’s Champions League, beating Barcelona 4-2 thanks to late goals from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz on Tuesday, while Liverpool clinched a dramatic comeback victory over Villarreal. Phil Foden scored a hat-trick as Manchester City thrashed AEK Athens 5-1, while there were also much-needed wins for Roma and Napoli. PSG kept their place at the top of the early league-phase table, but could yet count the cost of injuries suffered by Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at the Parc des Princes. Barcelona twice levelled against the two-time defending champions, but were ultimately well beaten as they slipped to their first defeat of the season. Hansi Flick’s men had won their previous 11 games in all competitions this term. Kvaratskhelia hit the post, Dembele hobbled off and Ferran Torres was denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia in a fast-paced opening. PSG took a deserved lead in the 38th minute as Desire Doue collected the ball outside the area and thumped a shot into the bottom corner. Garcia made another excellent save shortly after the break from Achraf Hakimi, before Xavi Espart burst through to level for Barca against the run of play. Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos both pulled up injured within seconds of each other and had to leave the field. The home team continued to press, though, and Lucas Hernandez restored their advantage 18 minutes from time with a brilliant header, shortly after former Barcelona forward Torres hit the post. Lamine Yamal powered past Warren Zaire-Emery to equalise again seven minutes later. But Vitinha hammered home from outside the box in the 81st minute and Ruiz’s tap-in gave Luis Enrique’s team a second straight 4-2 Champions League win after seeing off Man City by the same scoreline last week. – Liverpool fight back – Liverpool battled back from two goals down to also maintain their 100-percent record by edging out Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield. item.title: Tinubu mourns Afenifere leader Fasoranti
item.description: By Adeola Badru Afenifere has mourned its leader, Chief Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, recalling his contributions to Nigeria’s independence struggle, opposition to military rule and the campaign for the restoration of the annulled June 12, 1993 presidential election, as it described him as an exemplary leader whose life embodied patriotism, courage and service to humanity. The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation announced his passing in a statement issued on Tuesday by its National Publicity Secretary, Comrade Jare Ajayi, who said the centenarian, also known as Asiwaju Yoruba, died at about 4pm. Fasoranti, who turned 100 on May 11, 2026, was described by Afenifere as “a humanist, a philanthropist, an exemplary leader, a genuine patriot and a Yoruba leader and an icon” who remained a model of courage even in the most heart-rending circumstances. The organisation said the late elder statesman was the first of its leaders to attain the age of 100, having assumed the leadership of Afenifere in November 2008 following the death of his predecessor, Chief Abraham Adesanya, in August of the same year. According to the statement, Fasoranti followed in the footsteps of his predecessors by living an exemplary life from which individuals and organisations could draw inspiration and model their conduct. item.description: Vitinha’s superb late strike proved crucial as reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain saw off rivals Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday in a dramatic game between two of the leading contenders to win this season’s Champions League. It had briefly looked as though Barcelona would leave the French capital with a point when Lamine Yamal, who is hoping to win this year’s Ballon d’Or, stabbed in Barcelona’s second equaliser on the night. Desire Doue had earlier opened the scoring for PSG, and Lucas Hernandez got their second goal after teenager Xavi Espart found the net for the Catalans. The defeat is a setback for Barcelona, albeit not one that is likely to seriously hurt their prospects of advancing further in Europe’s elite club competition. They had travelled to France on a run of 11 consecutive wins at the start of the season in all competitions. item.title: FIFA U17 WWC: Flamingos beat Puerto Rico 2-0 to boost hopes
item.description: Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, boosted their chances at the ongoing FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco after securing a 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico in their Group B encounter in Rabat on Tuesday. The Flamingos, who won bronze at the 2022 edition of the competition, took the lead in the 25th minute through striker Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, who converted a pass from Queen Joseph. Nigeria started brightly, applying pressure on Puerto Rico’s defence and creating opportunities through quick passing and forward movement. Adegbuyi’s goal rewarded the team’s early efforts and gave Nigeria greater control of the game as the first half progressed. The Nigerian side continued to search for a second goal after the break, with Queen Joseph, Tosin Rafiu and Favour Nkwocha among those who threatened the Puerto Rican defence. Puerto Rico attempted to respond with tactical changes, but Nigeria coach Hakeem Busari also made substitutions to strengthen his team’s attacking options. Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku were introduced in the 67th minute as the Flamingos maintained their push for another goal. Their efforts paid off in the 90th minute when substitute Precious Oscar headed home a cross from Kemi Adegbuyi to double Nigeria’s lead and secure the victory. The Flamingos held on through six minutes of added time to claim all three points and strengthen their position in Group B. In the other group fixture, North Korea defeated Poland 6-1, setting up an important encounter with Nigeria on Friday. The result against Puerto Rico gives the Flamingos a boost ahead of the meeting with North Korea, which could prove crucial to their progress in the tournament. item.title: UK reaffirms commitment to deepen defence, security partnership with Nigeria
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The United Kingdom has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening its longstanding defence and security partnership with Nigeria, with renewed focus on military cooperation, professional military education, institutional capacity building and enhanced operational effectiveness. Director of Defence Information, Major General Samaila Uba said the commitment was reiterated when the recently appointed British High Commissioner to Nigeria, Mr. Pete Vowles, paid a courtesy visit to the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General OO Oluyede, at the Defence Headquarters, Abuja. The British High Commissioner expressed appreciation for the enduring political, diplomatic and military relations between both countries, emphasising that defence and security cooperation remain critical pillars of the UK-Nigeria bilateral relationship. He underscored his determination to sustain the momentum of existing security initiatives and explore opportunities to deepen collaboration in response to evolving regional and global security challenges. He further highlighted the importance of maintaining a strong and mutually beneficial partnership that support regional stability and strengthens Nigeria’s capacity to address contemporary security threats. In his response, the CDS highlighted the longstanding historical ties between Nigeria and the United Kingdom, noting that both countries have sustained a productive defence relationship for several decades and continued to work together in addressing shared security concerns. General Oluyede emphasised the importance of sustaining and expanding existing areas of cooperation, particularly in professional military education, transfer of technology and institutional capacity building. He noted that ongoing defence agreements and training programmes have contributed to enhancing the professional competence and operational capabilities of the Armed Forces of Nigeria. The CDS stressed that continued collaboration with strategic international partners remains important to strengthening the Armed Forces’ capacity to respond effectively to emerging threats, while promoting greater self-reliance, institutional resilience and operational efficiency. Both parties expressed optimism about the future of the UK-Nigeria defence and security partnership, reaffirming their commitment to building on existing achievements and identifying further areas of cooperation for mutual benefit. item.title: Ogun Assembly backs establishment of state police
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State House of Assembly has thrown its weight behind the proposed establishment of state police, passing a resolution in support of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026. The resolution, titled “H.R. No. 194/OG/2025 – Consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (1999) (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 (Establishment of State Police Services),” was passed during plenary, following the consideration of a report by the House Ad-hoc Committee on Constitutional Review. The committee, chaired by a former Speaker of the Assembly, Rt. Hon. Olakunle Oluomo, presented its report on 26 clauses and proposed amendments to various sections of the 1999 Constitution. Presenting the report, Oluomo took the proposed amendments one after another, with lawmakers voting in favour of all the clauses and sections contained in the proposals. The amendments covered various aspects of the bill, including the substitution, insertion and alteration of specific constitutional provisions aimed at providing a legal framework for the establishment of state police services. Following the consideration of the proposed amendments, Oluomo moved a motion for the adoption of the committee’s report. The motion was seconded by Hon. Adegoke Adeyanju and subsequently supported by the lawmakers through a voice vote. The House Leader, Hon. Yusuf Sherif, thereafter moved a motion for the adoption of the report as a resolution of the Assembly. The motion was seconded by the Chief Whip, Hon. Omolola Bakare, and unanimously supported by members through a voice vote. Speaking after the passage of the resolution, the Speaker of the Assembly, Rt. Hon. Oludaisi Elemide, said the Assembly had joined other state legislatures across the country in supporting the establishment of state police, describing the decision as historic. Elemide said the resolution reflected the position of the lawmakers and the people of Ogun State on the need to strengthen the country’s security architecture through the establishment of state police services. According to him, the initiative would help improve security measures and enhance the protection of lives and property, while promoting the social well-being and economic development of the state. He added that the proposed establishment of state police was an important step towards addressing security challenges and strengthening the capacity to safeguard communities. Following the passage of the resolution, the Speaker directed that a clean copy of the document be prepared and transmitted to the National Assembly to formally communicate Ogun State’s support for the proposed constitutional amendment. The resolution forms part of the ongoing constitutional amendment process through which state legislatures are considering proposed changes to the 1999 Constitution, including the proposal to establish state police services. item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government and Bi-Courtney Aviation Services Limited have signed a final settlement to end a nearly 20-year dispute over MMA2, paving the way for renewed revenue generation and the completion of abandoned hotel and conference centre projects in Lagos. Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Tuesday in Abuja during the formal signing of the agreement, saying the settlement would enable the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to begin receiving concession fees from MMA2 after years of litigation. Keyamo said the agreement followed the approval of the Federal Executive Council and the Federal Government’s decision under President Bola Tinubu to resolve the protracted dispute through negotiations rather than continued court battles. He described the settlement as a reciprocal arrangement under which both parties had agreed to relinquish outstanding claims to establish a framework for future cooperation. According to the minister, under the agreement, Bi-Courtney will waive its outstanding claims against the government, while the Federal Government and FAAN will release specified historical claims against the concessionaire, including accumulated concession fees and other related payments arising before the execution of the agreement. He noted that the resolution had been achieved without the Federal Government engaging external lawyers for the negotiations. Speaking at the event, Babalakin thanked President Tinubu and Keyamo for resolving the dispute, which he said had remained unresolved for more than 18 years despite the parties having maintained their respective positions. He said the settlement would create employment opportunities, particularly through the completion of the abandoned projects, while improving the appearance of the airport environment. According to him, the agreement would also encourage investors who have encountered disputes with government to consider negotiated solutions as a viable means of resolving disagreements. Babalakin assured the government, the ministry and FAAN that Bi-Courtney would honour its commitments under the agreement. item.title: Police rescue 11 Ghanaians lured to Nigeria with Canada visa offer
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State Police Command has rescued 11 Ghanaian nationals allegedly held against their will in Sagamu, Ogun State, after being lured to Nigeria with promises of Canadian and Spanish visas in a suspected international fraud scheme involving about ₦50.27 million. The victims, comprising seven males and four females, were rescued on October 19, following intelligence received by the police, according to a statement issued on Tuesday by the Command’s Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi. The statement said operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit swiftly mobilised to the suspected hideout after receiving actionable intelligence and successfully rescued all 11 victims. Preliminary investigations, according to the police, indicated that the victims were allegedly deceived by a fellow Ghanaian national who promised to facilitate their travel abroad. Each victim reportedly paid GH₵40,000 before being brought to Nigeria, where they were allegedly held against their will. However, the Command said investigations were ongoing to identify, track down and apprehend everyone connected with the alleged criminal network. The rescued Ghanaian nationals are receiving appropriate care and support, while detectives intensify efforts to unravel the circumstances surrounding their alleged ordeal. Reacting to the development, the Commissioner of Police in Ogun State, Bode Ojajuni, commended operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit for their prompt response and professionalism. Ojajuni reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives, combating transnational crime and preventing criminal networks from exploiting unsuspecting members of the public. He declared that the state would not provide a safe haven for individuals who prey on the hopes and trust of others. “There is no safe haven for criminals who exploit the hopes of others,” the police commissioner said. He assured residents and members of the public that the Command would sustain its efforts to ensure that those responsible for the alleged crime were brought to justice. The Command urged members of the public to exercise caution when dealing with individuals or agents offering overseas travel and visa-processing services. It advised prospective travellers to verify the authenticity of travel arrangements and the credentials of service providers before making payments. The police also encouraged the public to report suspicious activities that could help security agencies identify and disrupt criminal operations. Reiterating its commitment to intelligence-led policing and effective collaboration with other security agencies, the Command said it would continue to take decisive action against criminal networks operating within the state. “Every credible lead matters, every life matters, and protecting the public remains paramount,” the statement added. item.title: Cross River Assembly passes State Police Bill
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State House of Assembly, on Tuesday, threw its weight behind the creation of state police, passing the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, with all 22 members present voting in favour and none against, as lawmakers pushed for a decentralised policing system to tackle insecurity. Three of the Assembly’s 25 members were absent from plenary during the vote. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services in the country. It contains 26 clauses and proposes 25 alterations through substitutions to provisions of the principal Act, including Sections 84(4), 89(2), 121(3), 124(4), 109(2), 153(1), 157(2), 158(1) and 160. Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Elvert Ayambem, said the vote reflected the Assembly’s commitment to supporting constitutional reforms aimed at addressing security challenges and protecting lives and property. “By this vote, the 10th Assembly has demonstrated its support for the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, which seeks to establish a constitutional framework for State Police Services,” he said. He stressed that implementation of state policing must be guided by the rule of law, accountability and democratic principles. Contributing to the debate, the Leader of the House and member representing Odukpani State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Francis Asuquo, argued that policing must be brought closer to the people. He said a decentralised system would sharpen security responses and address challenges peculiar to grassroots communities. The member representing Yala I State Constituency, Hon. Brian Odey, called for effective coordination between state and federal security agencies, to ensure the proposed State Police Services complement existing security structures and improve overall operations. The Deputy Leader of the House and member representing Abi State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Davies Eta, insisted on adequate safeguards, accountability and professionalism. He said state police must operate within the confines of the law and respect the fundamental rights of citizens. Lawmakers also cited improved intelligence gathering and better protection of lives and property as key benefits of a decentralised policing system. The passage marks the Assembly’s formal endorsement of the proposed amendments, paving the way for the establishment of State Police Services in Nigeria. Ebola can cause fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting and diarrhoea. In severe cases, the disease can damage vital organs and cause bleeding. However, not everyone who contracts Ebola dies. Early diagnosis and appropriate medical care can improve the chances of survival. Scientists believe that fruit bats may be natural hosts of the Ebola virus, although its natural reservoir has not been definitively confirmed. Humans may become infected through contact with infected wild animals, including fruit bats, monkeys, chimpanzees, gorillas and other susceptible animals.
